items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: And he and Dick Nixon were friends and you know, they thought alike.

ctx.x: Well the shipyard we built into a big thing. It’s now the biggest shipyard on the west coast. And it was the biggest employer in San Diego at the time I left. We sold it to Kaiser Enterprises. And after a year and a half with Kaiser I decided I didn’t belong in

that big operation. So I told my good friend Edgar Kaiser I was going to leave, and did. And I went back with the guy who owned the shipyard in the first place, who now had a bank and a cannery and a bunch of tuna boats and the Yellow Cab Company in L.A. and San Francisco and a bus line in Kansas City. So I became the Executive Vice President of that company and ran all those businesses. And I was doing all right I guess. Then I discovered that there was some phony financing going on. I was on the board…
Well I can tell from your record collection that you must have been collecting all those years.
